# Bind tokens to one workspace

## Intent

A developer hands an agent a token that reaches one workspace and nothing else, so that a leaked or misused agent token cannot touch any other repository, any identity route or any other person's work. The hub confines such a token on every surface, reports each attempt to leave its workspace, and revokes it when its workspace goes away.

## Goals

- `POST /workspaces/:slug/tokens` mints a personal access token (PAT) bound to that workspace, atomically, and `GET /workspaces/:slug/tokens` lists the tokens bound to it.
- A binding guard runs for every bound PAT on every REST route and on git, after authentication and before the scope check, and answers `404 not_found` or `403 token_bound` for everything the binding does not cover.
- A token bound to a workspace reaches that workspace and the task forks created with it; a token bound to a task fork reaches the fork and, on the fork's parent, only the 25 contributor routes listed below.
- Each refusal is reported as `parley.token.bound_refused`, at most one event per token per minute, with the refusals in between counted as `suppressed`.
- Every live token bound to a workspace is revoked in the transaction that removes the workspace, and each maintenance pass revokes any live token whose workspace no longer exists.
- `parley tokens create --workspace <slug>` and `parley tokens list --workspace <slug>` call the two routes.
- Other packages get three components: one that mints a bound token inside their own transaction (fork creation, the hub credential of a sandbox), one that revokes the tokens bound to a set of workspaces inside their own transaction (workspace delete, fork expiry), and one that tells a route what the caller's binding covers.

## Background

The repository holds no code yet; every file named here is new, except that `internal/cli/tokens.go` and its test are first created by package 06 and extended here. The source is `docs/prd/03_platform.md`: PLAT-FR-080 to PLAT-FR-087, the two routes of §3.5, the two CLI entries of §3.6, the refusal limiter of §3.7, the two `parley.token.*` events of §3.8 and the bound-token edge cases of §3.10 (user story PLAT-US-04).

A PAT is the only credential that can carry a workspace binding (§3.3.2). Package 06 delivers the PAT with its `workspace` member (a slug or null, fixed at creation); package 07 delivers the workspace record and the access rule; package 02 delivers the position in the check order where the binding guard runs (step 5, after body checks and before the PAT scope check). This package fills that position and adds the two routes that create and list bound tokens.

The code lives in `internal/access/` (guard, coverage, minting, revoking, refusal limiter, sweep, the two route handlers) and in `internal/cli/tokens.go` (the `--workspace` flag).

## Requirements

### Binding (PLAT-FR-080)

A PAT may be bound to exactly one workspace. The binding is set when the token is created and never changes: no route changes a token's `workspace`, and a permission change by the owner leaves `workspace` and `paths` as they were (§3.10). A bound token is an ordinary PAT of the user who minted it. It has that user's access, cut down by the binding. The binding never grants access; it only removes it: if the owner loses access to the workspace, the bound token gets what the owner would get.

A bound token comes into being in three ways: through `POST /workspaces/:slug/tokens` (this package), through fork creation (package 15) and as the hub credential of a sandbox (package 45). All three go through one minting component of this package, which works inside the caller's transaction, applies the body validation and, for a PAT creator, the subset rule of package 06, writes the token with its binding and records `parley.token.bind` in the same transaction. If the transaction is rolled back there is no token and no event.

### Minting over REST (PLAT-FR-082, `POST /workspaces/:slug/tokens`)

The body is that of `POST /user/tokens`: `name` (1–255 characters), `permissions` (at least one registered scope), `paths` (optional), `expires` (0, 30, 60 or 90 days; default 90). The answer is `201` with the `Token` object, its `workspace` set to the slug and the member `token` holding the value `parley_pat_<token_id>_<secret>`. The value is shown in this response only. The route's need is `owner`.

Failures, in the order of checks:

| Caller or request | Answer |
|---|---|
| a bound PAT naming a workspace its binding does not cover | `404 not_found`, `workspace not found` |
| a bound PAT naming a workspace its binding covers | `403 token_bound` |
| an unbound PAT without `tokens:manage`, or asking for a permission or path it does not hold (subset rule) | `403 insufficient_scope` |
| no access to the workspace, or no such workspace | `404 not_found`, `workspace not found` |
| the admin token | `403 forbidden` |
| an org member who is not the owner | `403 forbidden` |
| a body that fails validation | `400 invalid_request` |
| the workspace is archived | `409 workspace_archived` |

Minting is atomic: either a bound token exists and is returned, or nothing was created. A token is never left unbound by a failure. A failure to record the bind event fails the request with `500 internal` and leaves no token.

The route takes `Idempotency-Key`. A replay answers `200` with the original token object without the `token` member (§3.10).

`parley.token.bind` carries: actor the minting user with actor type `api_key` or `pat`; resource type `token`, resource id the token id, action `bind`, workspace the bound slug; metadata `token_id`, `workspace`, `permissions`, `paths` (or null), `expires_at` (or null). It never carries the token value.

### Listing (PLAT-FR-084, `GET /workspaces/:slug/tokens`)

Answers `200` with a list of `Token` objects, oldest first: every token bound to the workspace, live, revoked or expired. No item carries a `token` member. The list follows the paging conventions (default limit 50). It works on archived workspaces. The need is `owner`; the admin token may list the bound tokens of any workspace. Failures: a bound PAT `403 token_bound` (or `404` outside its binding); an unbound PAT without `tokens:read` `403 insufficient_scope`; no access or no such workspace `404 not_found`; an org member `403 forbidden`.

### Coverage (PLAT-FR-081, PLAT-FR-063, §3.10)

A token bound to workspace W covers:

- W itself, in every state. Archiving does not touch bound tokens: the token still reaches an archived W and gets the routes' usual archived answers;
- every task fork of W that was created by a request authenticated with this token. The hub records the creating token on the fork. A fork of W that another user, or another token of the same user, created is not covered.

A token bound to a task fork F covers F. On F's parent P it reaches only the contributor routes of the next section.

For cross-workspace reads, the readable set of a bound PAT is the readable set of its user cut down to the covered workspaces.

### The binding guard (PLAT-FR-083, PLAT-FR-013 step 5)

The guard runs for bound PATs only. An API key, the admin token and an unbound PAT are never touched by it. It runs after authentication: a bound token's id with a wrong secret gets `401`, and an unknown path or a wrong method gets `404` or `405` as for any caller. It runs before the PAT scope check: a bound PAT without the route's scope on a workspace outside its binding gets `404`, not `403 insufficient_scope`.

| Request | Answer |
|---|---|
| names a workspace the binding covers | passes to the route's own checks; a route that declares that it refuses bound tokens answers `403 token_bound` |
| names the parent of the fork the token is bound to | the contributor routes pass to their own checks; every other route is `403 token_bound` |
| names any other workspace, existing or not | `404 not_found`, `workspace not found`, the same body in both cases |
| names no workspace and is on the allowlist | passes; the route confines its result to the covered workspaces |
| anything else, including every identity route | `403 token_bound` |

The allowlist: `GET /workspaces`, `GET /events`, `GET /events/log`, `GET /audit`, `GET /sandbox-profiles`, `POST /sessions`, `GET /sessions`, `GET /sessions/:id`, `POST /sessions/:id/complete`, `POST /sessions/:id/usage`, `GET /sessions/:id/usage`.

The contributor routes on the parent, all under `/workspaces/:slug` (from CHG-FR-040, LAND-FR-003, AWR-FR-001):

- changes: `POST /changes`, `GET /changes`, `GET /changes/:number`, `GET /changes/by-commit/:sha`, `PATCH /changes/:number`, `POST /changes/:number/abandon`, `POST /changes/:number/restore`, `POST /changes/:number/restack`, `GET /changes/:number/versions`, `GET /changes/:number/versions/:version`, `GET /changes/:number/diff`, `GET /changes/:number/stack`;
- landing and policy reads: `POST /changes/:number/land`, `GET /changes/:number/lands`, `GET /lands/:id`, `GET /changes/:number/conflict`, `GET /changes/:number/conflict/file`, `GET /changes/:number/approvals`, `GET /changes/:number/checks`, `GET /policy`, `POST /policy/evaluate`;
- awareness reads: `GET /activity`, `GET /changes/:number/overlaps`, `GET /claims`, `GET /claims/:id`.

A request that passes carries, for its handler, what the binding is: the bound slug and whether the named workspace is the bound one, a fork the token created, or the parent of the bound fork. The owning packages use it to confine a parent route to changes whose source is the fork.

Routes addressed with a fork's own slug that act on the parent's data (awareness and claims, forge, resolved variables) are routes of the fork and pass the guard.

A bound token's `tokens:*`, `keys:*`, `users:*` and `orgs:*` scopes have no use: identity routes answer it `403 token_bound`, including a token's attempt to read or revoke itself.

On git (`/git/:org/:slug.git/…`) the guard gives a decision for the slug: pass when the binding covers it, otherwise refuse with status `404`; package 17 writes the answer a git client reads.

### Refusal events (PLAT-FR-087, §3.7, §3.8)

Each request the guard refuses is reported as `parley.token.bound_refused`: actor the token's user with actor type `pat`; resource type `token`, resource id the token id, action `bound_refused`, workspace the bound slug; metadata `token_id`, `bound_workspace`, `requested_workspace` (only when the request named a workspace; the slug as the caller typed it), `method`, `route`, `status` (403 or 404), `surface` (`api` or `git`) and `suppressed` (an integer).

At most one event is emitted per token per minute. Refusals inside that minute emit nothing and are counted; the count is carried as `suppressed` on the token's next event and then starts again at 0. Tokens are limited independently. A request that passes the guard, a list that was filtered, and a request refused by another check (`401`, `403 insufficient_scope`, the access rule's `404`) are not refusals. The limiter state is in memory and is empty after a restart. A failure to emit never changes the HTTP answer.

### Removal of the workspace (PLAT-FR-085, PLAT-FR-086)

When a workspace is deleted or a task fork expires, every live token bound to it is revoked in the same transaction as the removal. The revoking component takes the slugs being removed, revokes each live token bound to one of them, and returns the revoked token ids sorted, for the removal's event. Tokens that are already revoked or expired are left as they are and are not returned. If the transaction is rolled back, no token was revoked. A revoked bound token answers `401 unauthenticated` from then on.

As a backstop, each maintenance pass runs the token binding sweep: it revokes every live token whose bound workspace no longer exists. Tokens bound to an existing workspace (archived ones included) and unbound tokens are not touched. A failing sweep returns its error to the maintenance loop and revokes nothing.

### CLI (§3.6)

- `parley tokens create --name <string> --permissions <list> [--paths <list>] [--expires <days>] --workspace <slug>` calls `POST /workspaces/<slug>/tokens` instead of `POST /user/tokens`, prints the `Token` with its value on stdout and warns on stderr that the value will not be shown again.
- `parley tokens list --workspace <slug>` calls `GET /workspaces/<slug>/tokens` instead of `GET /user/tokens` and prints the response body.

A hub error is printed on stderr as received and the command exits 1.

### End-to-end flows

1. **Mint and use.** A developer runs `parley tokens create --workspace W`; the CLI posts to the hub; the hub checks the caller, writes the token and the bind event in one transaction and answers `201`; the CLI prints the token. An agent then uses the value: a route of W passes the guard, a route of another workspace answers `404 workspace not found`, and `GET /user` answers `403 token_bound`.
2. **Refusal reporting.** An agent with a bound token calls routes outside its binding several times within a minute; the hub answers each one and emits one `parley.token.bound_refused`; after the minute the next refusal emits a second event whose `suppressed` is the number of refusals that were not reported.
3. **Sweep.** A bound token outlives its workspace record; the next maintenance pass revokes it; the agent's next request answers `401`.

## Design Decisions

1. **Where the code lives.** Guard, coverage, minting, revoking, limiter, sweep and the two route handlers are in `internal/access/`; the `--workspace` flag is added to `internal/cli/tokens.go` of package 06. Why: the brief's layout puts bound tokens in `internal/access`, and the same Go package as the access rule lets the readable set be cut down without an import cycle.
2. **The binding is stored as the slug**, as the PAT entity defines (`workspace`, a slug or null). The creating token of a fork is stored on the workspace record of package 07 as a nullable token id, added by this package and set by package 15. Why: PLAT-FR-081 says the hub records it on the fork.
3. **A token bound to a workspace that no longer exists** is not special-cased by the guard: a request naming that slug passes the guard and gets the access rule's `404`; every other workspace is `404` too. The sweep revokes it.
4. **"Names a workspace"** means that the matched route is under `/workspaces/:slug` (REST) or `/git/:org/:slug.git` (git). A slug in a query parameter or body is not seen by the guard; the allowlisted route confines it. Why: PLAT-FR-083 puts those routes on the allowlist and §14 gives them their own `404`.
5. **The contributor routes are one fixed table in this package**, matched by method and route pattern. Why: the PRD enumerates them (CHG-FR-040, LAND-FR-003, AWR-FR-001), and a fixed table can be tested before the routes exist.
6. **Routes that refuse every bound token declare it at registration**, and the guard answers `403 token_bound` at step 5, before the scope check. The two routes of this package use it; later packages use it for the routes the PRD marks "not a workspace-bound token". Outside the binding the `404` still comes first. Why: the PRD gives `403 token_bound` for these routes without placing it; step 5 is where every other `token_bound` is decided.
7. **On git every refusal is `404`**, also for the parent of the bound fork. Why: GIT-FR-003 names only `404` for the guard and §5 says the token "is answered like a stranger"; PLAT-FR-083's `403 token_bound` for the parent's other routes is read as applying to the REST API.
8. **Events are emitted through the event component of package 52** `durable_event_log_and_stream` (`internal/event`): `parley.token.bind` with its emit call that takes the caller's store transaction, so the token and its event commit together, and `parley.token.bound_refused` with its emit call that takes no transaction (`EmitNow`), as that package provides for a refused bound token. This package depends on package 52 and has no discarding fallback: the hub always passes the component. One Go constraint shapes the code: `internal/event` reads the workspace record of package 07 from `internal/access`, so `internal/access` cannot import `internal/event`. The guard and the minting component therefore call the component through a two-method interface declared in `internal/access` (`EventEmitter`: emit in a transaction, emit now), and `internal/hub/access.go` passes package 52's component behind it. Unit tests pass a recording implementation; the end-to-end checks run the real component and read the event log.
9. **The limiter's minute** starts when an event is emitted for the token; the clock is injectable. An entry whose minute has passed with a count of 0 is dropped at the next refusal of any token.
10. **`route` in the refusal event** is `/api/v1` followed by the pattern as registered with package 02's route registration, without the method (for example `/api/v1/workspaces/:slug/tokens`); for a request that matched no workspace it is still the matched pattern. Package 02 gives every check the matched route with its pattern and declarations.
11. **The hub credential of a sandbox appears in the list** like any bound token; "returned by no route" is read as its value. The minting component therefore takes an expiry instant, not only 0, 30, 60 or 90 days, for hub-internal callers.
12. **List order** is `created_at` ascending, then `token_id` ascending, because timestamps have whole seconds.
13. **The sweep and the revoking component emit no event of their own.** The removal's event carries `revoked_tokens`; the PRD defines no event for the sweep.
14. **`--workspace` with an empty value is a usage error** (exit 2, no request). Why: falling back to an unbound token would silently widen what the caller asked for.
15. **Tests** use the standard `testing` package with table-driven tests and `net/http/httptest`; the store is the embedded SQLite store of `internal/store` in a temporary directory (project decisions 2, 3, 7).
16. **Seams with earlier packages.** Minting calls the one minting operation of package 06 `api_keys_and_access_tokens` with the workspace binding and, for hub-internal callers, an expiry instant; this package does not validate or write a PAT by itself. The `--workspace` flag of both `parley tokens create` and `parley tokens list` is this package's, added to the commands package 06 created. The mark by which a route refuses every bound token is a named mark of package 02's route registration. The admin token on `POST /workspaces/:slug/tokens` gets `403 forbidden` with the message `this route needs a user`, the one message package 04 `authentication_and_login` gives the admin token wherever a user is needed; here it is answered by the handler, because the access check must run first. The sweep is registered under the maintenance task name `token_binding_sweep` that package 03 fixes. Wiring is in `internal/hub/access.go`.

## Dependencies

- Package 06 api_keys_and_access_tokens (draft): the PAT record with its `workspace` member, body validation, the subset rule, the scope check, revocation, the `parley tokens` commands.
- Package 07 workspace_access_rule (draft): the workspace record (slug, owner, org, kind, parent), the access rule with need `owner`, the readable set.
- Package 09 cli_foundation (draft): the command helper, the client with its segment encoder, the printers and the exit codes the `--workspace` flag is built on.
- Package 52 durable_event_log_and_stream (draft): the event component in `internal/event` with its two emit calls, through which `parley.token.bind` and `parley.token.bound_refused` are written.
- Through them: package 02 (check order position 5, the matched route and its named marks, error envelope, lists, idempotency), package 03 (store, the maintenance task registry with the fixed task name `token_binding_sweep`, the composition in `internal/hub/`), package 04 (authentication of the PAT).

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Task fork (fork)**: A workspace created from another workspace (its parent) for one task. It shares history with the parent, has its own branches and expires: after 7 days by default, or 24 hours after all its changes have landed or been abandoned.
- **Change**: The unit of work: a proposal to add the commits of a source branch to a target branch, with a number, a title, an intent, versions and a state.
- **Scope / permission**: A string carried by a PAT that grants read or write access to an area.
- **Bound token**: A PAT confined to one workspace (and the forks created with it). A token bound to a fork also reaches its own changes, and the awareness and policy reads, on the fork's parent (§3).
- **Path-scoped token**: A PAT whose writes are limited to files matching a list of globs.
- **Hub credential**: The fork-bound PAT the hub mints for a sandbox so that it can reach the hub. The workload sees only its placeholder, in `PARLEY_API_KEY`.
- **Hub event**: A record of something the hub did (`parley.*` types), with a sequence number. Hub events form the audit log and the event stream.
- **Binding guard**: The check that confines a bound PAT, run after authentication on every REST route and on git.
- **Covered workspace**: A workspace a binding reaches in full: the bound workspace and the task forks created with the token.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Minting a bound token over REST

**Rationale:** A developer needs one call that yields a token for an agent which is bound from the first moment, and never a token that exists without its binding.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN the owner of a workspace that is not archived sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/tokens with an API key, or with an unbound PAT that holds tokens:manage and every requested permission, and a body that passes the validation of POST /user/tokens, THE parleyd SHALL create a PAT owned by the caller's user and bound to that workspace, and return the token object with its value
   → HTTP 201 with a Token object {token_id, user_id, name, permissions, paths, workspace, expires_at, revoked_at, created_at, token}: workspace equals the slug, user_id is the caller's user, revoked_at is null, paths is null when the body gave none, expires_at is created_at plus the body's expires in days (90 when absent, null when 0), and token matches ^parley_pat_[a-z0-9]{8}_[a-z0-9]{32}$ with token_id as its middle part; a later request that presents token is authenticated as that PAT
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub handler built from the server pipeline of internal/server with authentication, the scope check and the access rule installed, a store in t.TempDir(), a recording event emitter, user alice with an API key, and workspace w1 owned by alice
   ```
   in internal/access/bound_tokens_test.go, a table over callers {alice's API key, alice's unbound PAT with [tokens:manage, git:read]} and bodies {{name:'agent', permissions:['git:read']}, the same with expires:0, the same with expires:30 and paths:['docs/**']}: r = post('/api/v1/workspaces/w1/tokens', body); assert r.status == 201; assert r.json.workspace == 'w1'; assert r.json.user_id == alice.id; assert r.json.revoked_at == null; assert r.json.token matches the pattern and contains r.json.token_id; assert r.json.expires_at == null for expires 0, else created_at + days; assert the store holds one PAT with that token_id whose workspace is 'w1'; assert authenticate(r.json.token).token_id == r.json.token_id
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN a bound token is minted through POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/tokens, THE parleyd SHALL record exactly one parley.token.bind event in the same store transaction as the token
   → one event handed to the event emitter with type parley.token.bind, workspace the bound slug, actor_id the minting user, actor_type api_key or pat according to the calling credential, resource_type token, resource_id the token id, action bind, and metadata {token_id, workspace, permissions, paths (or null), expires_at (or null)}; no member of the event holds the token value or its secret part
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub handler built from the server pipeline of internal/server with authentication, the scope check and the access rule installed, a store in t.TempDir(), a recording event emitter, user alice with an API key, and workspace w1 owned by alice
   ```
   in internal/access/bound_tokens_test.go, a table over callers {API key, unbound PAT with tokens:manage and git:read}: r = post('/api/v1/workspaces/w1/tokens', {name:'agent', permissions:['git:read']}); evs = emitter.events(); assert len(evs) == 1; e = evs[0]; assert e.type == 'parley.token.bind' and e.workspace == 'w1' and e.actor_id == alice.id; assert e.actor_type == 'api_key' or 'pat' per the caller; assert e.resource_type == 'token' and e.resource_id == r.json.token_id and e.action == 'bind'; assert e.metadata == {token_id: r.json.token_id, workspace:'w1', permissions:['git:read'], paths:null, expires_at:r.json.expires_at}; assert the JSON of e does not contain r.json.token nor its secret part; assert the emitter received the event with the same transaction the token row was written in
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF writing the token or recording the parley.token.bind event fails while POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/tokens is being served, THEN THE parleyd SHALL roll back the whole mint and answer with a hub failure, leaving neither a token nor an event
   → HTTP 500 with error_type internal and a message that does not contain the cause; the store holds no new PAT, bound or unbound; no parley.token.bind event was committed
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub handler built from the server pipeline of internal/server with authentication, the scope check and the access rule installed, a store in t.TempDir(), a recording event emitter, user alice with an API key, and workspace w1 owned by alice
   ```
   in internal/access/bound_tokens_test.go, a table over the failing step {the event emitter returns errors.New('emitter down'), the token insert fails}: before = count(PATs); r = post('/api/v1/workspaces/w1/tokens', validBody); assert r.status == 500; assert r.json.error.error_type == 'internal'; assert not contains(r.body, 'emitter down'); assert count(PATs) == before; assert count(PATs where workspace is null) is unchanged; assert emitter.committed() is empty
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] IF the owner sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/tokens with a body that fails the validation of POST /user/tokens, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request and create nothing
   → HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_request; the store holds no new PAT and no event is recorded

### REQ-2: One minting component and a binding that never changes

**Rationale:** Fork creation and the sandbox's hub credential must mint bound tokens under the same rules and inside their own transactions, and a token's binding must be a fact nobody can edit afterwards.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN another component of the hub calls the minting component of internal/access inside a store transaction with an owner, the creating credential, a workspace slug, a name, permissions, paths and an expiry given in days or as an instant, THE parleyd SHALL write a PAT of that owner bound to the slug and record parley.token.bind through the event emitter in that same transaction, and return the token object and its value to the caller
   → returns (Token, value, nil) with Token.workspace equal to the slug and Token.expires_at equal to the given instant or to now plus the given days (null for 0 days); when the caller commits, the store holds the token and the emitter holds one parley.token.bind event for it; when the caller rolls back, the store holds no such token and the emitter holds no committed event
   Check: integration
   - setup: a store in t.TempDir() with user alice and workspace w1; a recording event emitter that tracks the transaction of each event
   ```
   in internal/access/mint_test.go, a table over {commit, rollback} x {expiry 30 days, expiry instant now+2h, expiry 0}: tx = store.begin(); tok, value, err = MintBound(ctx, tx, {owner: alice, creator: alice's API key, workspace:'w1', name:'hub', permissions:['git:read','git:write'], paths:null, expiry}); assert err == nil; assert tok.workspace == 'w1'; assert tok.expires_at per the case; assert value contains tok.token_id; commit or roll back; on commit assert store.pat(tok.token_id).workspace == 'w1' and emitter.committed() has one parley.token.bind with resource_id tok.token_id; on rollback assert store.pat(tok.token_id) is absent and emitter.committed() is empty
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] IF the minting component is called with a name, permissions, paths or expiry in days that fail the validation of package 06, or with a PAT as the creating credential that does not hold a requested permission exactly or whose paths do not cover the requested paths, THEN THE parleyd SHALL return the error of package 06 for that case and write nothing in the caller's transaction
   → returns an error that the server pipeline renders as HTTP 400 invalid_request (validation) or HTTP 403 insufficient_scope naming the first offending permission or path (subset rule); no token row and no event were written in the transaction
   Check: unit
   - setup: a store in t.TempDir() with user alice and workspace w1; a recording event emitter
   ```
   in internal/access/mint_test.go, a table over {name '', permissions [], permissions ['nope:x'], days 45, creator PAT [git:write] asking git:read, creator PAT with paths ['src/**'] asking paths null, creator PAT with paths ['src/*'] asking ['src/**']}: tx = store.begin(); _, _, err = MintBound(ctx, tx, input); assert err != nil; assert errorType(err) == 'invalid_request' for the first four and 'insufficient_scope' for the others; assert count(PATs in tx) == 0; assert emitter.events() is empty
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] WHEN a caller repeats a successful POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/tokens within 24 hours with the same Idempotency-Key header and the same body, THE parleyd SHALL answer with the original token object without its value and mint nothing
   → HTTP 200 with the body of the first response minus the member token; the store still holds exactly one PAT bound to the workspace and the emitter holds exactly one parley.token.bind event
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub handler built from the server pipeline of internal/server with authentication, the scope check and the access rule installed, a store in t.TempDir(), a recording event emitter, user alice with an API key, and workspace w1 owned by alice
   ```
   in internal/access/bound_tokens_test.go: h = {'Idempotency-Key': 'k1'}; r1 = post('/api/v1/workspaces/w1/tokens', body, h); r2 = post('/api/v1/workspaces/w1/tokens', body, h); assert r1.status == 201 and r2.status == 200; assert 'token' not in r2.json; assert r2.json == r1.json without 'token'; assert count(PATs where workspace == 'w1') == 1; assert len(emitter.events()) == 1
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] THE parleyd SHALL for any bound token, keep its workspace and its paths unchanged through every route that changes or reads a token

   Check: integration

### REQ-4: What a binding covers

**Rationale:** The promise of a bound token is that it reaches its workspace and the forks made with it and that every other workspace does not exist for it.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN a bound PAT sends a request to a route under /api/v1/workspaces/:slug whose slug is the workspace the token is bound to, in any state of that workspace including archived, THE parleyd SHALL pass the request to the route's own checks and give its handler the binding: the bound slug and the relation bound
   → the response is the one the route gives an unbound PAT of the same user with the same permissions; the handler reads {bound_workspace: slug, relation: bound} from the request context; no parley.token.bound_refused event is emitted
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub handler with authentication, the binding guard, the scope check and the access rule installed, a store in t.TempDir(), a recording event emitter, and a probe route GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/probe with need read and scope git:read that answers 200 with the binding it finds in the request context

   in internal/access/guard_test.go, a table over workspaces {w1 active, w2 archived}: b = get('/api/v1/workspaces/' + slug + '/probe') with the PAT bound to slug; u = the same with alice's unbound PAT [git:read]; assert b.status == 200 and u.status == 200; assert b.json.binding == {bound_workspace: slug, relation: 'bound'}; assert u.json.binding == null; assert emitter.events() is empty
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] WHEN a bound PAT sends a request that names a task fork of the workspace it is bound to, and the fork's record names this token as the token that created it, THE parleyd SHALL pass the request to the route's own checks and give its handler the binding with the relation created_fork
   → the probe answers HTTP 200 with binding {bound_workspace: the parent's slug, relation: created_fork}; no parley.token.bound_refused event is emitted
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub handler with authentication, the binding guard, the scope check and the access rule installed, a store in t.TempDir(), a recording event emitter, and a probe route GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/probe with need read and scope git:read that answers 200 with the binding it finds in the request context

### REQ-5: A fork-bound token on the fork's parent

**Rationale:** An agent working in a task fork must be able to open, follow and land its own changes in the parent and see what others are doing there, and must be able to do nothing else in the parent.

   → the route's handler runs and reads {bound_workspace: the fork's slug, relation: parent_of_bound_fork} from the request context; the response is the handler's; no parley.token.bound_refused event is emitted
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub handler with authentication, the binding guard, the scope check and the access rule installed, a store in t.TempDir(), a recording event emitter, and a probe route GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/probe with need read and scope git:read that answers 200 with the binding it finds in the request context
   - setup: alice owns p1 and its fork f1; tokF is bound to f1 with every scope the routes need; the test registers each of the 25 method-and-pattern pairs with a probe handler
   ```
   in internal/access/guard_test.go, a table with one row per contributor route (25 rows, method and concrete path on p1 such as GET /api/v1/workspaces/p1/changes/7/versions/2): r = request with tokF; assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.binding == {bound_workspace:'f1', relation:'parent_of_bound_fork'}; assert emitter.events() is empty; assert the table has 25 rows and each row's pattern is in the guard's contributor list
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] IF a PAT bound to a task fork sends a request that names the fork's parent on any route that is not one of the 25 contributor routes, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request before the scope check and the access rule run
   → HTTP 403 with error_type token_bound; the route's handler does not run

[REQ-5.3] IF a PAT bound to a registered workspace, or to a fork, sends a request on a contributor route that names a workspace other than the parent of the fork it is bound to, THEN THE parleyd SHALL apply the coverage rule alone, so that the contributor routes open nothing but the bound fork's own parent
   → HTTP 404 with error_type not_found and message workspace not found for: a token bound to fork f1 of p1 on GET changes of another workspace p2, a token bound to p1 on GET changes of p2, and a token bound to fork f1 on GET changes of f1's sibling fork

### REQ-6: The binding guard on every other route and on git

**Rationale:** A leaked agent token must not read or change its owner's identity, mint further tokens or reach the hub's cross-workspace routes beyond what its workspace needs.

#### Criteria

1. ### REQ-7: Reporting refusals as rate-limited events

**Rationale:** A refused request from a bound token is a sign of a confused or compromised agent that the workspace owner wants to see, without one looping agent flooding the event log.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] WHEN the binding guard refuses a request of a bound PAT and no parley.token.bound_refused event was emitted for that token in the preceding 60 seconds, THE parleyd SHALL emit one parley.token.bound_refused event for the refusal through the event emitter
   → one event with type parley.token.bound_refused, workspace the bound slug, actor_id the token's user, actor_type pat, resource_type token, resource_id the token id, action bound_refused, and metadata {token_id, bound_workspace, method, route, status, surface, suppressed}: route is the route pattern the router matched, status is the HTTP status the guard answered (403 or 404), surface is api or git, suppressed is 0 for a token's first event; metadata has requested_workspace, holding the slug exactly as the caller typed it, only when the request named a workspace
   Check: integration
   - setup: the hub handler of the guard tests with a recording event emitter and a refusal limiter whose clock the test advances; tokA and tokB are bound to w1
   ```
   in internal/access/refusal_test.go, a table over refusals by a fresh token {GET /api/v1/workspaces/w5/probe -> status 404, requested_workspace 'w5'; GET /api/v1/workspaces/NoSuch/probe -> 404, 'NoSuch'; GET /api/v1/user -> 403, no requested_workspace member; POST /api/v1/workspaces/w1/tokens -> 403, 'w1'; GuardGit on w5 -> 404, surface git}: evs = emitter.events(); assert len(evs) == 1; e = evs[0]; assert e.type == 'parley.token.bound_refused' and e.workspace == 'w1' and e.actor_id == alice.id and e.actor_type == 'pat' and e.resource_type == 'token' and e.resource_id == tok.token_id and e.action == 'bound_refused'; assert e.metadata.status, surface, method per the row; assert e.metadata.route == the matched pattern (for example '/api/v1/workspaces/:slug/probe'); assert e.metadata.suppressed == 0; assert ('requested_workspace' in e.metadata) per the row; also: a limiter built anew (as after a restart) emits on its first refusal
   ```
1. [REQ-7.2] WHILE less than 60 seconds have passed since a parley.token.bound_refused event was emitted for a token, THE parleyd SHALL emit no event for a further refusal of that token and add 1 to the token's count of suppressed refusals
   → the event emitter receives nothing for the refusal; the HTTP answer of the refused request is the same as for a reported one
   Check: integration
   - setup: the hub handler of the guard tests with a recording event emitter and a refusal limiter whose clock the test advances; tokA and tokB are bound to w1

1. [REQ-7.3] WHEN the binding guard refuses a request of a bound PAT 60 seconds or more after the last parley.token.bound_refused event of that token, and refusals were suppressed in between, THE parleyd SHALL emit one event whose suppressed member is the number of refusals not reported since the previous event, and start the count again at 0
   → the second event of the token has metadata.suppressed equal to the number of suppressed refusals and otherwise describes the refusal that triggered it; an event emitted after a further 60 seconds with no refusal in between has suppressed 0
   Check: integration
   - setup: the hub handler of the guard tests with a recording event emitter and a refusal limiter whose clock the test advances; tokA and tokB are bound to w1

   in internal/access/refusal_test.go: refuse tokA at t0, t0+1s, t0+30s, t0+59s, then at t0+60s; evs = emitter.events(); assert len(evs) == 2; assert evs[1].metadata.suppressed == 3; assert evs[1].metadata.route and status describe the request at t0+60s; refuse tokA at t0+120s; assert emitter.events()[2].metadata.suppressed == 0

### REQ-8: Revoking bound tokens when their workspace is removed

**Rationale:** A token must not outlive the workspace it was made for, and the removal and the revocation must not be separable by a crash.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-8.1] WHEN a component that removes workspaces (workspace delete, fork expiry) calls the revoking component of internal/access inside its store transaction with the slugs being removed, THE parleyd SHALL revoke every live token bound to one of those slugs in that transaction and return the revoked token ids
   → returns the ids of the tokens it revoked, sorted ascending, as a non-nil list that is empty when there were none or when no slug was given; after commit each returned token has revoked_at set to the time of the call; tokens that were already revoked or expired keep their revoked_at and are not returned; tokens bound to other workspaces and unbound tokens are unchanged
   Check: integration
   - setup: a store in t.TempDir(); w1 has two live bound tokens, one revoked and one expired; fork f1 has one live bound token; w5 has one live bound token; alice has one unbound token; an injectable clock
   ```
   in internal/access/revoke_test.go, a table over slug lists {['w1'], ['w1','f1'], ['w3'] (no bound token), []}: tx = store.begin(); ids, err = RevokeBoundTo(ctx, tx, slugs); tx.commit(); assert err == nil; assert ids != nil; assert ids == sorted ids of the live tokens bound to the slugs; for each id assert store.pat(id).revoked_at == now (whole seconds); assert the already revoked token of w1 keeps its earlier revoked_at and is not in ids; assert the expired token of w1 has revoked_at == null and is not in ids; assert the token bound to w5 and alice's unbound token have revoked_at == null
   ```
1. [REQ-8.2] IF the transaction in which the revoking component was called is rolled back, or the component's own write fails, THEN THE parleyd SHALL leave every token as it was before the call
   → after a rollback no token's revoked_at has changed; when its write fails the component returns a non-nil error and a nil list, and the caller's transaction can still be rolled back
   Check: integration
   - setup: the store of the previous check; a store wrapper that fails updates on demand
   ```
   in internal/access/revoke_test.go, a table over {caller rolls back after a successful call, the store fails the update}: before = snapshot(revoked_at of every PAT); tx = store.begin(); ids, err = RevokeBoundTo(ctx, tx, ['w1']); for the failing store assert err != nil and ids == nil; tx.rollback(); assert snapshot(revoked_at of every PAT) == before
   ```
1. [REQ-8.3] WHEN a request presents a bound token after the transaction that revoked it was committed, THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request at authentication on every route
   → HTTP 401 with error_type unauthenticated on a route of the token's former workspace, on a route of another workspace and on an allowlisted route; no parley.token.bound_refused event is emitted
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub handler with authentication, the binding guard, the scope check and the access rule installed, a store in t.TempDir(), a recording event emitter, and a probe route GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/probe with need read and scope git:read that answers 200 with the binding it finds in the request context

   ```

### REQ-9: The token binding sweep

**Rationale:** If a removal ever leaves a bound token behind, the token must stop working within one maintenance interval and not stay live for ever.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-9.1] WHEN the token binding sweep runs, THE parleyd SHALL revoke, in one store transaction, every live token whose bound workspace has no workspace record, and report how many it revoked
   → returns (n, nil) where n is the number of tokens revoked; each of them has revoked_at set to the time of the sweep; a second sweep right after returns (0, nil)
   Check: integration
   - setup: a store in t.TempDir() holding: two live tokens bound to slug 'gone' (no workspace record); one live token bound to active w1; one live token bound to archived w2; one live unbound token; one revoked and one expired token bound to 'gone'; an injectable clock
   ```
   in internal/access/sweep_test.go: n, err = SweepBindings(ctx); assert err == nil and n == 2; assert store.pat(orphan1).revoked_at == now and store.pat(orphan2).revoked_at == now; assert the PATs of the next criterion are unchanged; n2, _ = SweepBindings(ctx); assert n2 == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-9.2] THE parleyd SHALL for any token that is unbound, or bound to a workspace that has a record in any state including archived, or already revoked or expired, leave the token unchanged when the token binding sweep runs
   Check: same as REQ-9.1
1. [REQ-9.3] IF the store fails while the token binding sweep runs, THEN THE parleyd SHALL roll the sweep back and return the failure to the maintenance loop
   → returns (0, err) with a non-nil error; no token's revoked_at has changed; the function returns and does not terminate the process
   Check: unit
   - setup: the store of the previous check wrapped so that it fails updates on demand
   ```
   in internal/access/sweep_test.go: before = snapshot(revoked_at of every PAT); n, err = SweepBindings(ctx) on a store wrapper that fails the second update; assert err != nil and n == 0; assert snapshot == before
   ```
1. [REQ-9.4] WHEN a maintenance pass of parleyd runs, THE parleyd SHALL run the token binding sweep as the maintenance task named token_binding_sweep
   Check: same as PATH-3

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A developer mints a bound token from the CLI and an agent is confined by it

1. **developer** runs parley tokens create --name agent --permissions git:read --workspace w1 with an API key
2. **parley CLI** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/w1/tokens with the body built from the flags
3. **parleyd** authenticates the API key, finds the caller is the owner of w1, writes the bound token and the parley.token.bind event in one transaction and answers 201
4. **parley CLI** prints the token object with its value on stdout and the show-once warning on stderr
5. **agent** presents the token value on a route of w1, on a route of another workspace of the same owner and on GET /api/v1/user
6. **parleyd** passes the first request to the route, answers the second 404 workspace not found and the third 403 token_bound
7. **developer** runs parley tokens list --workspace w1 and sees the token without its value

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parley CLI command tree and HTTP client, HTTP server pipeline of internal/server, authentication, scope check, workspace access rule, binding guard, bound-token routes, store, the event component of internal/event (package 52)

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a store in a temporary directory, user alice with an API key, and the workspaces w1 and w5 owned by alice
- the test registers one probe route GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/probe (need read, scope git:read) to stand for the workspace routes of later packages; events go to the real event component of package 52, and the test reads them back from its event log by position

**End state:**

- the CLI's stdout parses as a Token whose workspace is w1 and whose token authenticates
- with that token the probe answers 200 on w1 and 404 not_found on w5, and GET /api/v1/user answers 403 token_bound
- parley tokens list --workspace w1 prints one item with that token_id and no token member
- the event log of package 52 holds one parley.token.bind event for the token

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/bound_tokens_test.go: out = parley('tokens','create','--name','agent','--permissions','git:read','--workspace','w1'); tok = json(out.stdout); assert out.code == 0 and tok.workspace == 'w1'; assert get('/api/v1/workspaces/w1/probe', tok.token).status == 200; r = get('/api/v1/workspaces/w5/probe', tok.token); assert r.status == 404 and r.json.error.error_type == 'not_found'; u = get('/api/v1/user', tok.token); assert u.status == 403 and u.json.error.error_type == 'token_bound'; l = json(parley('tokens','list','--workspace','w1').stdout); assert len(l.items) == 1 and l.items[0].token_id == tok.token_id and 'token' not in l.items[0]; assert the event log read through internal/event holds one parley.token.bind with resource_id tok.token_id
```

### PATH-2: An agent leaves its binding repeatedly and the owner gets rate-limited refusal events

1. **agent** sends three requests with a bound token within one minute: to another workspace, to an unknown slug and to GET /api/v1/user/tokens
2. **parleyd** answers 404, 404 and 403 token_bound from the binding guard, emits one parley.token.bound_refused event for the first refusal and counts the other two
3. **agent** sends one more request to another workspace after the minute has passed
4. **parleyd** answers 404 and emits a second parley.token.bound_refused event with suppressed 2

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** HTTP server pipeline of internal/server, authentication, binding guard, refusal limiter, store, the event component of internal/event (package 52)

**Setup:**

- the in-process hub of PATH-1 with the event component of package 52 and a limiter clock the test advances
- a token bound to w1

**End state:**

- the four responses are 404, 404, 403 and 404
- the event log holds exactly two parley.token.bound_refused events for the token; the first has suppressed 0, the second has suppressed 2, and both have workspace w1

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/bound_tokens_test.go: assert get('/api/v1/workspaces/w5/probe', tok).status == 404; assert get('/api/v1/workspaces/nosuch/probe', tok).status == 404; assert get('/api/v1/user/tokens', tok).status == 403; clock.advance(61s); assert get('/api/v1/workspaces/w5/probe', tok).status == 404; evs = the events of type parley.token.bound_refused read from the event log through internal/event; assert len(evs) == 2; assert evs[0].metadata.suppressed == 0 and evs[1].metadata.suppressed == 2; assert evs[0].workspace == 'w1' and evs[0].metadata.requested_workspace == 'w5'
```

### PATH-3: A maintenance pass revokes a token whose workspace is gone

1. **agent** holds a live token bound to a workspace whose record was removed without revoking the token
2. **parleyd** runs a maintenance pass, which runs the task named token_binding_sweep and revokes the token
3. **agent** sends a request with the token
4. **parleyd** answers 401 unauthenticated

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** maintenance task registry, token binding sweep, authentication, HTTP server pipeline of internal/server, store

**Setup:**

- the in-process hub of PATH-1 with its maintenance tasks registered as parleyd registers them
- a live token bound to w1 and a live token bound to slug 'gone', which has no workspace record (the test removes the record directly in the store)

**End state:**

- after one maintenance pass the token bound to 'gone' has revoked_at set and a request with it answers 401
- the token bound to w1 still answers 200 on the probe route of w1
- the registry lists a task named token_binding_sweep

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/bound_tokens_test.go: assert 'token_binding_sweep' in hub.maintenance.taskNames(); hub.maintenance.runPass(ctx); r = get('/api/v1/workspaces/gone/probe', orphanTok); assert r.status == 401 and r.json.error.error_type == 'unauthenticated'; assert get('/api/v1/workspaces/w1/probe', liveTok).status == 200
```


# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `go test ./... -count=1`
- **linter:** `golangci-lint run ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/access/... ./internal/cli/... ./test/e2e/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `06` — mints through its one minting operation with a workspace binding, and uses the PAT record with its workspace member, the subset rule, the scope check and the parley tokens commands the --workspace flag is added to
- `07` — uses the workspace record, the access rule with need owner and the readable set it cuts down
- `09` — builds its CLI commands on the client, output and exit-code helpers of the CLI foundation
- `52` — emits parley.token.bind inside the minting transaction and parley.token.bound_refused without one through the two emit calls of its event component

## Tasks

### 1. Record what a binding covers and cut the readable set down to it (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-4.6

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the coverage behaviours to internal/access/coverage_test.go as table-driven tests against a store in t.TempDir() and confirm they fail
- 1.2 Add a schema migration that gives the workspace record of package 07 a nullable creating-token id, and a store function that sets it when a workspace row is inserted; package 15 calls it at fork creation, the tests call it directly
- 1.3 Define the Binding value in internal/access: the bound slug and the relation of the named workspace to it, one of bound, created_fork and parent_of_bound_fork, with functions that put it into and read it from a request context
- 1.4 Add CoveredSet: for a PAT bound to W return W and every fork of W whose creating-token id is this token's id, sorted; for a PAT bound to a fork return the fork alone; a bound slug with no workspace record yields the slug alone
- 1.5 Add the relation lookup the guard will use: given a bound PAT and a slug, answer bound, created_fork, parent_of_bound_fork or none, reading the workspace record's kind and parent on every call so that nothing is cached between requests
- 1.6 Extend the readable set of package 07 so that for a bound PAT the result is the readable set of the token's user intersected with CoveredSet, and is unchanged for an API key, the admin token and an unbound PAT
- 1.7 Declare the EventEmitter interface in internal/access with the two emit calls of package 52's event component (emit inside a given store transaction; emit now, in a transaction of its own), because internal/event imports internal/access and cannot be imported back; give it no discarding default, and add a recording implementation in a test helper file that remembers each event and the transaction it came with

**Touches:**

- `internal/access/binding.go`
- `internal/access/coverage.go`
- `internal/access/coverage_test.go`
- `internal/access/events.go`
- `internal/access/testing_test.go`

**Done when:**

- the checks of the criteria listed above exist as tests, are executable and pass

### 2. Guard routes that name a workspace, including the fork's parent (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-4.1, REQ-4.2, REQ-4.3, REQ-4.4, REQ-4.5, REQ-5

**Steps:**

- 2.1 Add the workspace-route behaviours to internal/access/guard_test.go and confirm they fail; build the test hub from the server pipeline of internal/server with authentication, the scope check and the access rule installed, and register probe routes that answer the binding found in the request context
- 2.2 Implement the binding guard as the check that package 02 runs at position 5 (after body checks, before the PAT scope check): it does nothing for an API key, the admin token and an unbound PAT
- 2.3 A request names a workspace when its matched route pattern lies under /api/v1/workspaces/:slug; take the slug from the path value exactly as typed
- 2.4 When the relation is bound or created_fork, put the Binding into the request context and pass the request on
- 2.5 Hold the 25 contributor routes of the PRD as one fixed table of method and route pattern relative to /api/v1/workspaces/:slug; when the relation is parent_of_bound_fork pass a request whose method and matched pattern are in the table, with the Binding in its context, and answer every other request 403 token_bound
- 2.6 When the relation is none answer 404 not_found with the message workspace not found, through the same error helper the access rule of package 07 uses, so that the body is the same for an existing and for an unknown slug
- 2.7 Make no access or scope decision in the guard: a passed request goes on to the scope check and the access rule unchanged, so a bound token never gets more than an unbound PAT of the same user
- 2.8 Call a refusal reporter (an interface with a discarding default, filled by the next tasks) once for each 403 and 404 the guard answers, with the token, the bound slug, the typed slug, the method, the matched pattern, the status and the surface api

**Touches:**

- `internal/access/guard.go`
- `internal/access/guard_test.go`
- `internal/access/contributor_routes.go`
- `internal/access/testing_test.go`

### 4. Report guard refusals as rate-limited events (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-7

**Steps:**

- 4.1 Add the refusal-event behaviours to internal/access/refusal_test.go with a recording event emitter and a clock the test advances, and confirm they fail
- 4.2 Implement the refusal limiter as the guard's refusal reporter: in-memory state per token id holding the time of the last emitted event and the count of suppressed refusals, guarded for concurrent requests, with an injectable clock
- 4.3 On a refusal with no event for the token in the preceding 60 seconds, build parley.token.bound_refused (workspace the bound slug, actor the token's user with actor type pat, resource token and the token id, action bound_refused, metadata token_id, bound_workspace, method, route, status, surface, suppressed) and hand it to the event emitter; set the count to 0 and the time to now
- 4.4 Put requested_workspace into the metadata only when the request named a workspace, holding the slug as typed; route is the matched route pattern as registered, without the method
- 4.5 On a refusal inside the 60 seconds emit nothing and add 1 to the count; the count is carried as suppressed on the token's next event
- 4.6 Emit after the response decision and never let the emit change it: recover from a panic of the emitter, ignore its error, log it once at warn level without the token value, and do not retry
- 4.7 Drop a token's entry when its 60 seconds have passed and its count is 0, at the next refusal of any token, so the map does not grow with tokens that stopped being refused
- 4.8 Create the limiter in internal/hub/access.go with package 52's event component as its event emitter (the refusal event uses the emit call without a transaction) and pass it to the guard and to GuardGit; the state is not persisted, so a restart starts empty

**Touches:**

- `internal/access/refusal.go`
- `internal/access/refusal_test.go`
- `internal/access/guard.go`
- `internal/hub/access.go`

**Done when:**

- the checks of the criteria listed above exist as tests, are executable and pass

### 5. Mint bound tokens through one component and POST /workspaces/:slug/tokens (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1, REQ-2.1, REQ-2.2

**Depends on:** 1

**Steps:**

- 5.1 Add the minting behaviours to internal/access/mint_test.go and internal/access/bound_tokens_test.go and confirm they fail
- 5.2 Implement the minting component MintBound: inside the store transaction it is given, call the one minting operation of package 06 with the workspace binding set to the slug (it validates name, permissions, paths and expiry, applies the subset rule when the creating credential is a PAT and writes the token), and emit parley.token.bind through the event emitter, which is package 52's event component, with that same transaction
- 5.3 Accept the expiry either as 0, 30, 60 or 90 days (0 meaning never) or as an instant for hub-internal callers; return the token object and its value, and return package 06's errors unchanged so that the pipeline renders 400 invalid_request and 403 insufficient_scope
- 5.4 Build the bind event with workspace the bound slug, actor the owner with actor type api_key or pat from the creating credential, resource token and the token id, action bind, and metadata token_id, workspace, permissions, paths or null, expires_at or null; never put the value or its secret part into it
- 5.5 Register POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/tokens with scope tokens:manage, need owner, the mark that it refuses bound tokens, and token declared as its show-once member for idempotent replays
- 5.6 In the handler, after the pipeline's checks: answer the admin token 403 forbidden with the message "this route needs a user", the one message package 04 gives the admin token, before reading the body's content; then validate; then answer 409 workspace_archived for an archived workspace; then open one transaction, call MintBound, commit and answer 201 with the token object and its value
- 5.7 On any failure of the insert, the event emitter or the commit, roll back and answer 500 internal without the cause, so that no token exists without its binding and none exists without its event
- 5.8 Register the route on the hub's composition in internal/hub/access.go and pass it package 52's event component as the event emitter
